query: For refractory high-entropy alloys intended for structural use under extreme-temperature conditions, what single intervention could improve high-temperature oxygen resistance? State one hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains its mechanism, predicts the improvement relative to the untreated alloy, defines the temperature, atmosphere, and exposure conditions under which it should work, cites supporting prior evidence, and proposes an experiment with a clear result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Severe surface deformation to generate an ultrafine-grained microstructure will enhance the formation of protective oxide scales and reduce oxidation kinetics in a refractory HEA.
generation.material_initial_state: An as-cast AlCoCrFeNi refractory high-entropy alloy with a coarse-grained microstructure.
generation.intervention: Application of severe friction processing (e.g., multi-pass stationary friction treatment) to induce an ultrafine-grained surface layer.
generation.conditions: Isothermal oxidation at 1100 °C in air for 100 hours.
generation.structural_mediator: An ultrafine-grained surface microstructure with high grain boundary density that promotes uniform and rapid formation of a continuous protective oxide scale (e.g., Al2O3 and Cr2O3 layers).
generation.mechanism: Refinement of the grain structure increases the density of diffusion paths (grain boundaries) facilitating the rapid nucleation and growth of protective oxide scales, thereby reducing oxygen ingress and oxidation kinetics.
generation.predicted_outcome: A reduction in oxidation rate by approximately 40–50% (as measured by parabolic rate constants) relative to the as-cast coarse-grained alloy.
generation.baseline: The as-cast AlCoCrFeNi alloy exhibiting higher oxidation weight gain and non-uniform oxide scale formation under the same conditions.
generation.boundary: The beneficial effects are expected at 1100 °C in dry air and for exposure times around 100 hours; effects may diminish if the ultrafine-grained layer is too thin or if severe deformation adversely affects surface integrity.
generation.uncertainty: The long-term stability of the ultrafine-grained layer at high temperatures and any potential negative impacts on mechanical properties require further investigation.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of AlCoCrFeNi HEA samples: one set is processed by severe friction processing to achieve an ultrafine-grained surface layer, and the other set remains in the as-cast condition. Both sets will undergo oxidation at 1100 °C in air for 100 hours.
measurements: TGA to compare oxidation kinetics and mass gain.
EBSD/SEM to verify grain size refinement and oxide scale uniformity.
XRD to identify protective oxide phases.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the processed samples do not display a statistically significant reduction (around 40–50%) in oxidation rate or fail to form a denser protective oxide scale in comparison with the as-cast samples, the hypothesis is falsified.

cited_evidence.text: It is worth mentioning that all the prior studies on microstructural refinement and the oxidation behavior of the resulting materials were limited to conventional structural materials only. To the best of the authors’ knowledge, there has been no study on achieving remarkable oxidation resistance in HEAs through microstructural refinement. In the current work, microstructural refinement of the AlCoCrFeNi HEA was accomplished via severe surface deformation using stationary friction processing (SFP). The processing resulted in ultrafine-grain structure with a significant fraction of nanograins in the as-cast HEA along with significant elemental homogenization. The processed HEA samples demonstrated exceptional oxidation resistance, and the reported mass gain values are among the lowest for the investigated HEA. The remarkable performance of the processed HEAs was attributed to the formation of an intact, dense, uniformly distributed oxide scale, favored by large grain boundary density, higher surface free energy, and uniform elemental distribution.

A coarse grain microstructure having BCC/B2 phases was obtained in the as-cast HEA sample. Only 5 min of straining of sample significantly refined the grain structure from 98 to 1 μm and 0.43 μm for the SFP_400 and SFP_1800 sample, respectively. The ultrafine-grained samples showed a phase transition from BCC/B2 to FCC structure. The SFP_400 sample showed a 12–20% reduction in the oxidation kinetics, whereas the SFP_1800 sample showed a 38–48% reduction in the oxidation kinetics compared to the as-cast alloy. Low values of parabolic rate constant and high values of activation energy for the ultrafine-grained samples show the high oxidation resistance of the processed samples. Protective oxide scales of Al2O3 and Cr2O3 were predominantly found after discontinuous isothermal oxidation. Other than protective scales, the availability of Co(Cr,Fe)2O4 spinel phases was also observed during the oxidation at elevated temperatures. The presence of more GBs favoring outward flux of elements to form a dense chromia layer followed by internal Al-rich oxide layered structure is responsible for the enhanced oxidation resistance of the processed samples.

papers.title: Fluorine Effect for Improving Oxidation Resistance of Ti-45Al-8.5Nb Alloy at 1000 °C.
papers.approach: A two‐step spraying and isothermal oxidation process with fluorine treatment
papers.findings: Fluorine-treated specimens formed a dense, continuous Al2O3 film that reduced weight gain from 6.03 mg/cm² (untreated) to 0.81 mg/cm² after oxidation at 1000 °C for extended durations (up to 100 h).
papers.mechanism: Fluorine promotes selective oxidation; its presence (as volatile aluminum-fluoride species) leads to rapid formation and adhesion of a protective Al2O3 scale, suppressing TiO2 formation nearby.

papers.title: An oxidation resistant refractory high entropy alloy protected by CrTaO<sub>4</sub>-based oxide.
papers.system: Refractory high-entropy alloy (RHEA) containing refractory elements with relatively low Ti content
papers.approach: Long-term isothermal oxidation experiments at 1000 °C and 1100 °C (up to 200 h) to study mass gain behavior and oxide layer evolution
papers.findings: At 1100 °C, the alloy formed an external protective oxide layer largely based on CrTaO4 (with some Cr2O3 and Al2O3 dispersion) that limited weight gain to as low as 4.03 mg/cm² after 200 h, outperforming comparable alloys tested for 48 h.
papers.mechanism: The formation of a CrTaO4-based oxide, promoted by lower Ti content, acts as a diffusion barrier to oxygen and elemental out-diffusion, stabilizing the oxide layer over long exposures.

papers.title: Effect of Al Addition on Microstructure and Properties of CoCrNi Medium-Entropy Alloy Prepared by Powder Metallurgy.
papers.system: CoCrNi medium‐entropy alloy with varied Al content
papers.approach: Powder metallurgy processing followed by systematic variation of Al content to evaluate formation of oxide phases
papers.findings: When Al content exceeds a threshold (≥0.5 molar ratio), a continuous alumina (Al2O3) scale forms during high-temperature oxidation (e.g., at 1100 °C), leading to significant improvements in oxidation resistance as evident from lower mass gains.
papers.mechanism: Aluminum enriches the surface and reacts to form a protective, adherent Al2O3 scale that limits further oxygen ingress.

papers.title: Microstructure and Composition Evolution of a Fused Slurry Silicide Coating on MoNbTaTiW Refractory High-Entropy Alloy in High-Temperature Oxidation Environment.
papers.system: MoNbTaTiW refractory high-entropy alloy with a silicide coating
papers.approach: Application of a Si-20Cr-20Fe silicide coating via a fused slurry method followed by high-temperature oxidation studies
papers.findings: The silicide coating effectively delayed oxidation by forming a layered oxide structure during exposure at high temperatures, with the coating’s microstructure evolving to form an outer oxide and an inner silicide layer that shifted toward the substrate.
papers.mechanism: The silicide coating supplies Si (and Cr) that diffuses to form protective silicides and corresponding oxides, thereby hindering oxygen transport and substrate oxidation.

papers.title: Preparation of VZrHfNbTa High-Entropy Alloy-Based High-Temperature Oxidation-Resistant Coating and Its Bonding Mechanism.
papers.system: VZrHfNbTa refractory high-entropy alloy with a high-temperature oxidation-resistant Hf coating
papers.approach: Application of a Hf-based coating on the HEA surface followed by isothermal oxidation at extreme temperatures (around 1873 K) in air
papers.findings: Coated samples exhibited a significantly lower weight gain per unit area compared to uncoated ones, with the Hf coating forming a dense HfO2 layer after oxidation which effectively limited further oxidation.
papers.mechanism: The Hf coating oxidizes to form HfO2, a highly stable and dense oxide that acts as an effective diffusion barrier against oxygen ingress during prolonged high-temperature exposure.

papers.title: Effect of Cr on Microstructure and Properties of WVTaTiCrx Refractory High-Entropy Alloy Laser Cladding.
papers.approach: Laser cladding fabrication with systematic variation of Cr content and subsequent oxidation tests at 800 °C for 50 h
papers.findings: Addition of Cr significantly reduced oxidation weight gain; the optimal Cr composition (Cr1) led to ~5.12 mg/cm² weight gain and an oxidation rate reduced by over 50% compared to the Cr-free variant.
papers.mechanism: Cr facilitates the formation of protective Cr-based oxide phases that slow down oxidation kinetics by acting as barriers to oxygen diffusion.

papers.title: Enhanced Oxidation Resistance of Ultrafine-Grain Microstructure AlCoCrFeNi High Entropy Alloy.
papers.system: AlCoCrFeNi high-entropy alloy processed to attain an ultrafine-grained microstructure
papers.approach: Severe surface friction processing (SFP) to produce an ultrafine-grained microstructure followed by high-temperature oxidation tests
papers.findings: Ultrafine-grained samples exhibited a 38–48% reduction in oxidation kinetics relative to as-cast material, attributed to the formation of a dense, layered oxide scale (with inner Al2O3 and outer Cr2O3 layers) under oxidation conditions typically around 900–1100 °C.
papers.mechanism: Grain refinement increases the density of grain boundaries that facilitate rapid and uniform formation of protective oxide scales, thereby reducing oxygen permeation and overall oxidation rate.

established: Protective, continuous oxide scales (e.g., Al2O3, Cr2O3, HfO2, CrTaO4) are key to high-temperature oxidation resistance.
Alloying elements such as Al and Cr, when incorporated either in the bulk or via surface coatings, can promote formation of these protective oxides.
Surface treatments (coatings or modifications) and microstructural modifications (e.g., grain refinement) have been shown to improve oxidation kinetics in high-temperature environments.

approaches_tried.outcome: Induced selective oxidation leading to formation of a protective Al2O3 film; significantly reduced oxidation weight gain in TiAl alloys.

approaches_tried.approach: Alloying additions (Al, Cr) in medium-/high-entropy alloys
approaches_tried.outcome: Enhanced protective oxide formation (Al2O3, Cr2O3) resulting in improved oxidation resistance at temperatures around 1100 °C.
Creation of dense, protective oxide layers (e.g., HfO2 or silicide-derived oxides) which markedly reduce oxidation rates under extreme conditions.

approaches_tried.approach: Microstructural refinement via severe surface deformation
approaches_tried.outcome: Ultrafine grain structures that aid formation of uniform and adherent oxide scales, reducing oxidation kinetics by up to ~48%.

mechanisms: Formation of a continuous, adherent oxide film (e.g., Al2O3, Cr2O3, HfO2) acts as a barrier to oxygen diffusion.
Surface treatments (halogen or coating-based) modify elemental diffusion behavior, favoring selective oxidation.
Microstructural refinement increases grain boundary density, promoting rapid and uniform oxide scale formation.
disagreements: Some studies note that while certain alloying additions (e.g., Al, Cr) improve oxidation resistance, they can also lead to the formation of brittle intermetallic phases that compromise mechanical properties.
There is discussion regarding the role of minor elements (e.g., Ti); while necessary for some alloy systems, excessive Ti can impede formation of a protective oxide layer by promoting TiO2 growth.
open_questions: What is the optimal single intervention for refractory high-entropy alloys that combines high-temperature oxidation resistance without compromising mechanical integrity?
Can treatments such as halogen surface modification (shown effective in TiAl alloys) be effectively transferred to refractory HEA systems?
How do long-term (>200 h) oxidation behaviors of these interventions compare under extreme temperature and operational environments?
opportunities: Investigate a single, minimalistic surface intervention—such as a targeted Hf-based coating—in refractory HEAs to promote in situ formation of a protective HfO2 scale.
Explore applying halogen (fluorine) treatments on refractory HEA surfaces to see if the mechanism of selective oxidation and protective film formation observed in TiAl alloys can be replicated.

Combine optimal surface coatings with microstructural refinement to achieve synergistic improvements in oxidation resistance under extreme temperature, air (or dry oxygen) conditions for extended durations.
Perform systematic studies varying processing parameters (temperature, exposure time, atmosphere composition) to map the stability and failure modes of the protective oxide scales formed.

directions.direction: Halogen (fluorine) surface modification of the HEA to promote selective oxidation.
directions.assessment: Directly targets the formation of a protective oxide film by locally accelerating selective oxidation of Al to Al2O3. Supported by evidence in TiAl alloys (PMC9030595) and considered transferable with careful process control, although the effect in refractory HEAs remains somewhat uncertain.

directions.direction: Application of a Hf-based coating on the HEA surface.
directions.assessment: Utilizes an external Hf coating that forms a dense, stable HfO2 scale at high temperatures. There is strong evidence in refractory HEA systems (PMC10488483) and it directly improves oxygen resistance without altering the bulk composition.

directions.direction: Application of a silicide-based coating (e.g., Si-20Cr-20Fe) on the HEA.
directions.assessment: Forms a layered oxide/silicide structure on oxidation that impedes oxygen diffusion. This method is well‐documented (PMC7475834) although processing complexity and scale adhesion need careful control.

directions.direction: Inducing an ultrafine‐grained microstructure via severe surface plastic deformation.
directions.assessment: Refines the surface grain structure to accelerate the formation of continuous protective oxides owing to increased grain boundary density. Evidence in high-entropy alloys (PMC9026100) supports improved kinetics although applicability to refractory HEAs under extreme conditions may vary.

candidates.intervention: A controlled fluorine treatment applied by spraying or dipping in a low-concentration NH4F solution, followed by a brief drying period.

candidates.hypothesis: A thin Hf-based coating will improve high-temperature oxygen resistance of a refractory HEA by forming a protective HfO2 layer.
candidates.intervention: Deposition of a ~5–10 μm Hf coating via physical vapor deposition (PVD) onto the alloy’s surface.

candidates.hypothesis: A silicide coating (Si-20Cr-20Fe) applied on a refractory HEA will lead to the formation of a layered protective oxide scale that enhances oxygen resistance.
candidates.intervention: Application of a fused slurry silicide coating with a Si-20Cr-20Fe composition to create an initial bilayer structure.
